rows.what_the_ink_shows: At the top, the quotient is written A_n = A/(F with superscript n+1, V with superscript n+1). Both superscript groups extend beyond the initial n and terminate in a raised 1; the F superscript is more heavily inked, while the V group is more separated (crops/9_scan007_L769_quotient_exponents.jpg). This is compatible with and supports the supplied n+1 check. In the middle, A_n est fini sur W_n is written, and the alternative dualizing functor has target Hom over W_n-modules of (M,W_n); the nearby parenthetical condition uses F^n,V^n (crops/9_scan007_L769_Wn_dualizing_functor.jpg). In the final underlined isomorphism, the Hom base and its second argument visibly read W_n, with no +1 after either n (crops/9_scan007_L769_final_isomorphism.jpg).
rows.note: The manuscript juxtaposes the n+1 quotient exponents with W_n in the duality formula. The current TeX preserves precisely those indices, with existing doubt marks around the top exponents, so no transcription correction to W_{n+1} is warranted. Retain all bytes and existing doubt marks. The supplied editorial refinement proposes A_n isomorphic to Hom over W_{n+1} of (A_n,W_{n+1}), or alternatively redefining A_n as A/(F^n,V^n) when retaining W_n. Its supplied reason is that p^n times 1 is nonzero in A/(F^{n+1},V^{n+1}), because the ideal's constant terms lie in p^{n+1}W, so the quotient is not a W_n-module. This explanation is recorded as the supplied mathematical index-slip diagnosis; it was not independently proved here. The row's earlier 600-dpi check and reference to Michel Hua's project are supplied prior evidence, not a claim that I produced a new 600-dpi source or consulted that project. Medium confidence reflects the small heavily inked top exponent, not uncertainty about the clearly written W_n in the final target.
